newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends mainly up, but spot month slumps.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends mainly up, but spot month slumps.

text.p: CSCE coffee prices posted slight gains on Tuesday, with the exception of the spot September contract, which fell sharply on heavy speculative liquidation a day ahead of its expiry, trading sources said.
In what one trader termed a "last-minute, get-me-out" scramble, September delivery slid 3.90 cents a lb, to 112.20 cents, with the bulk of the selling occuring during the last few minutes of trading.
Today's action lopped 4.40 cents off September's premium to second-position December, but its margin remained a relatively steep 6.35 cents heading into the Wednesday's expiry.
Aside from spot-month adjustments, activity in the futures market was subdued. Benchmark December futures rose half a cent on the day, to close at 105.85, down from a briefly held peak of 107.25.
December briefly crossed Monday's intraday high of 106.80, a minor resistance area, but was unable to muster enough buying enthusiasm to pierce stiff resistance at 108 cents.
Even widely-watched supply figures released late yesterday lacked market-moving punch, dealers said.
U.S. warehouse stocks of green coffee fell in August to their lowest level in seven years, the Green Coffee Association reported, but most operators took the news in stride.
"The GCA numbers were in line with expectations," said one. "The market appears stuck and going nowhere."

With new-crop beans starting to flow in from Central and South America, warehouse stocks are expected to build steadily during the next few months. Current low levels of consumer stocks have long been factored into prices, traders said, noting the spot month's longstanding premium to the deferreds.

In other news, an official with the International Coffee Organization said he expected world coffee consumption to grow at an annual rate of 2.5 percent annually through 2000. Pablo Dubois, speaking to delegates to the F.O. Licht coffee conference in Hamburg, stressed that his forecast was a personal estimate and not an official ICO projection.
-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640
